name: Omani Empire (East African coast)
alt: African dominion of the Sultan of Muscat

predecessors.name: Sultanate of Oman
predecessors.text: the Tanzanian and Kenyan coast that Cliopatria draws inside its Sultanate of Oman shapes from 1744 to 1814

successors.name: Sultanate of Zanzibar (to 1890)
successors.text: the African section of the empire, 'ruled by Majid bin Said' as the Sultanate of Zanzibar after the division of 1856

ledger.x: 1814: the Omani coast of East Africa appears as its own dominion.
25 July 1826: the British protectorate over Mombasa ends and Omani rule is restored through liwalis.
June 1837: the vassal relation ends in annexation (see the gain below).
1840: Said bin Sultan moves his capital from Muscat to Stone Town, Zanzibar ('In 1840, Said moved his capital from Muscat to Stone Town in Zanzibar'); the Omani Empire infobox says 1832.
January 1844: Said's army lands at Faza against Siyu and Pate.
19 October 1856: the Omani Empire is divided between Said's sons.

wars.name: Omani bombardment of Mogadishu
wars.outcome: Omani suzerainty over the Banadir restored: 'Thus Mogadishu was bombarded by Omani forces in 1828 and the Banadir Omani suzerainty was restored', after an incident in 1823 in which two community leaders aboard an Omani ship were kidnapped.

wars.name: Omani expedition against Siyu and Pate
wars.outcome: Failure: a force of about 2,000 landed at Faza in January 1844 and withdrew without a victory; Amir Hemed was killed at Siyu in 1845.

certainty.note: The coast is a string of towns and claims: no treaty or survey fixes a boundary in the pages opened.
